signal: VertexOne launched VXconnect, a modern customer engagement engine for energy and utility providers (May 2025)

email.body1:
Andrew, saw VertexOne launched VXconnect to modernize how utilities engage their customers.

A launch like that opens a lot of utility accounts at once, usually more than the team can personally cover before they cool off. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for VertexOne off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Andrew, quick follow-up for VertexOne.

A new product usually expands the in-market list faster than headcount can keep up, and the coverage gap shows up late as a missed quarter. Most utility-tech teams never map how many meetings they actually need to hit the number.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings VertexOne needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Andrew, last bit of proof for VertexOne.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how VertexOne's reply rate likely compares to other utility-tech vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Andrew, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Rolling out a new engagement platform is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a utility-tech motion? I'll tailor it to VertexOne either way.
